title: Expectation deviation and nonconstant Fourier mass
statement: Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that is $\varepsilon$-biased, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The absolute difference between the $\phi$-weighted expectation of $f$ after identifying the Boolean cube with the sign cube, and the uniform mean of $f$, is at most $\bigl(\|\widehat f\|_1-|\widehat f(\varnothing)|\bigr)\varepsilon$, where $\|\widehat f\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute Fourier coefficients and $\widehat f(\varnothing)$ is the constant Fourier coefficient.
